about: Existing-object boundary: additive narrowing lowers finite interval freedom; exact withdrawal and witnessed local widening can reopen it without creating a coordinate. Research comparison only; different hypotheses do not establish a fork.

branches.publishedStatement: the freedom of a system is the sum of its cells' debits in bits; an encounter never raises it; only a new coordinate does

freedom is log₂ of the states between the poles, which is the cell's entropy: encounters lower it, vacuity raises it, and nothing else moves it; two paths interfere from phase alone, and that is lost once which path was taken is observed
